lines.trans: Listen here, I am not going to figure anything out.
Vika, Sasha has absolutely nothing to do with this.
Do not fire her from this job.
I was intentionally driving you to anger.
I pretended as if we were dating.
Well, you did a very good job with it.
Especially when you grabbed her by the chest.
Believe me, it was just a stupid accident!
And why are you sticking up for her so much?
I am not sticking up for her at all now.
I just do not want anyone to get hurt.
Because of what? Because of that exact thing.

meanings.note: Coordinating or subordinating Russian conjunction meaning 'and', linking clauses in spoken dialogue.
Secondary conversational sense ('so, and what about') (starting a question: а жвачку?) used in spoken Russian dialogue.

examples.trans: Dad, did you bring any gum?

meanings.note: Coordinating or subordinating Russian conjunction meaning 'as if', linking clauses in spoken dialogue.

examples.text: Он смотрит, как будто знает всё.
examples.trans: He looks as if he knows everything.

examples.text: Ты смотришь на меня так, как будто убить хочешь.
examples.trans: You look at me as if you want to kill me.

meanings.note: the present tense is normally left out: я мэр = I am the mayor
Secondary conversational sense ('there is, there are') (present есть; у меня есть = I have) used in spoken Russian dialogue.
future: буду / будешь ... + infinitive

examples.trans: You will be asking for forgiveness.

встречаться.gloss: to meet; to date, to go out

meanings.en: to date, to go out (with someone)
meanings.note: Prefix 'вс-' ('up') marks upward or sudden onset of action (stem 'тречаться'). Used in Russian as an imperfective verb expressing ongoing, habitual, or repeated action meaning 'to meet', forming an aspectual pair with 'встретиться'. The reflexive suffix '-ся'/'-сь' makes the action intransitive, reciprocal, or directed at the subject.
Secondary conversational sense ('to meet up') (+ с + instrumental) used in spoken Russian dialogue.

examples.trans: We've been dating for a month.
We've been going out for a month already.

выяснять.gloss: to find out, to clarify, to sort out

meanings.note: выяснять отношения = to hash out relationship issues, to argue

examples.trans: And then sort out your relationship!

examples.text: Не надо выяснять отношения на улице.
examples.trans: Don't hash out your relationship in the street.

examples.text: Слушай сюда, я не собираюсь ничего выяснять.
examples.trans: Listen here, I am not going to figure anything out.

meanings.note: Agrees in gender, number, and case with the noun it modifies ('stupid, silly, foolish').

examples.text: Ваня, ты глупый? Зачем ты сейчас это при нём сказал?
examples.trans: Vanya, are you stupid? Why did you just say that in front of him?

meanings.note: Common masculine noun meaning 'anger, wrath' in everyday Russian.

examples.text: Это я тебя специально доводил до гнева.
examples.trans: I was intentionally driving you to anger.

meanings.note: Common masculine noun meaning 'chest, breast' in everyday Russian.

examples.text: Особенно когда ты её за грудь хватал.
examples.trans: Especially when you grabbed her by the chest.

examples.text: А что вы так грубо разговариваете?
examples.trans: Why are you talking so rudely?

meanings.note: Russian preposition meaning 'until' that governs a specific oblique case on the following noun phrase.
Secondary conversational sense ('goodbye') used in spoken Russian dialogue.
Prefix 'до-' marks reaching a boundary or finishing the remainder of an action (stem 'водить'). Used as an imperfective (ongoing/repeated action) verb meaning 'to drive (to), bring (to)'.

examples.text: Это я тебя специально доводил до гнева.
examples.trans: I was intentionally driving you to anger.

examples.text: Не надо каждый раз доводить шефа до крика.
examples.trans: You should not drive the chef to shouting every time.

meanings.note: Russian preposition meaning 'for' that governs a specific oblique case on the following noun phrase.
Secondary conversational sense ('behind') (+ instrumental) used in spoken Russian dialogue.

заступаться.gloss: to stand up for, to defend

meanings.en: to stand up for someone, intercede
meanings.note: Prefix 'за-' marks beginning an action, covering, or stopping by along the way (stem 'ступаться'). Used in Russian as an imperfective verb expressing ongoing, habitual, or repeated action meaning 'to stand up for', forming an aspectual pair with 'заступиться'. The reflexive suffix '-ся'/'-сь' makes the action intransitive, reciprocal, or directed at the subject.

examples.trans: After all, he stood up for her!
The brother always stands up for his sister.

examples.text: А что ты за неё так заступаешься?
examples.trans: And why are you sticking up for her so much?

meanings.note: Russian preposition meaning 'because of' that governs a specific oblique case on the following noun phrase.
Secondary conversational sense ('from behind') (+ genitive) used in spoken Russian dialogue.

examples.text: Из-за вашей Лёли весь класс зовёт меня врунишкой!
examples.trans: Because of your Lyolya the whole class calls me a little liar!
We were late because of the rain.

examples.text: А трава в мешках сгорела. Из-за вас!
examples.trans: And the herbs in the sacks burned. Because of you!

meanings.note: Prefix 'из-' ('out from within') marks extraction or exhaustion (stem 'ображать'). Used as an imperfective (ongoing/repeated action) verb meaning 'to portray, pretend'.

examples.text: Я изображал, будто мы с ней встречаемся.
examples.trans: I pretended as if we were dating.

examples.text: Я весь вечер изображал, будто мы с ней встречаемся.
examples.trans: All evening I pretended as if she and I were dating.

examples.text: Не надо изображать из себя великого ресторанного критика.
examples.trans: Do not play the part of a great restaurant critic.

meanings.note: Invariable Russian adverb used to modify verbs or whole clauses with the sense 'when'.

examples.trans: When I grow up, I'll be the mayor.

examples.text: Когда ты наконец принесёшь горячий соус на раздачу?
examples.trans: When will you finally bring the hot sauce to the pass?

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian pronoun ('someone') whose case form reflects its grammatical role in the clause.

examples.trans: Finally someone is for the people!

examples.text: Слушай, тут пишут: «Гордость России! Наконец-то кто-то за народ!»
examples.trans: Listen, here they write: 'Pride of Russia! Finally someone is for the people!'

examples.text: Ты что, не понимаешь? Я задавить кого-то мог!
examples.trans: Don't you understand? I could have run someone over!

meanings.note: нас = us (gen/acc/prep); у нас = we have, at our place
Secondary conversational sense ('other forms:  (gen/acc),  (dat),  (instr),  (prep)') used in spoken Russian dialogue.

examples.text: Смотрите, какой у нас грязный унитаз!
examples.trans: Look, how dirty our toilet is!

meanings.en: must, need to, it is necessary
meanings.note: Manner or predicative adverb in '-о' derived from the corresponding adjective stem, used in everyday speech to mean 'it is necessary'.

examples.trans: We need to do even more.

meanings.note: goes right before the word it negates
+ genitive: ни копейки = not a penny
Secondary conversational sense ('...  = neither... nor') used in spoken Russian dialogue.

examples.text: Пятьсот. А у меня ни копейки.
examples.trans: Five hundred. And I haven't got a penny.

meanings.note: usually in the genitive ничего, with не: ничего не осталось

examples.text: Ну что, очкарик? Видишь, ничего не осталось.
examples.trans: Well, four-eyes? See, there's nothing left.

meanings.note: hesitation, at the start of a sentence
Secondary conversational sense ('oh come on!') (ну, папа!) used in spoken Russian dialogue.

examples.text: Ну что, очкарик? Видишь, ничего не осталось.
examples.trans: Well, four-eyes? See, there's nothing left.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian pronoun ('she') whose case form reflects its grammatical role in the clause.

examples.text: Паша, я больше не хочу о ней слышать. Понял?
examples.trans: Pasha, I don't want to hear about her again. Understood?

meanings.note: Manner/predicative adverb in '-о', derived from the neuter short form of the corresponding adjective.

examples.trans: It is especially cold outside today.

examples.text: И, Марина Сергеевна, читайте всё внимательно! Особенно мелким шрифтом!
examples.trans: And, Marina Sergeyevna, read everything carefully! Especially in fine print!

meanings.note: Invariable Russian adverb used to modify verbs or whole clauses with the sense 'very'.
Secondary conversational sense ('very much') (with verbs: очень люблю) used in spoken Russian dialogue.

examples.trans: I love our town very much.

examples.text: Я очень люблю наш город. Поэтому я иду на второй срок.
examples.trans: I love our town very much. That's why I'm running for a second term.

meanings.note: + dative of the person: поверить ему

examples.text: Со своего телефона? И все поверили?
examples.trans: From your own phone? And everyone believed it?

получиться.gloss: to turn out, to work out

meanings.en: to turn out, to work out
meanings.note: Prefix 'по-' forms perfective verbs or marks a brief/onset action (stem 'лучиться'). Used in Russian as an perfective verb focusing on a single completed action or result meaning 'to turn out', forming an aspectual pair with 'получаться'. The reflexive suffix '-ся'/'-сь' makes the action intransitive, reciprocal, or directed at the subject.

meanings.en: to come out of, to make
meanings.note: из тебя получится мэр = you'll make a mayor

examples.text: Классный из тебя мэр получится, Самсон.
examples.trans: You'll make a great mayor, Samson.

meanings.note: Prefix 'по-' forms perfective verbs or marks a brief/onset action (stem 'страдать'). Used as an perfective (single completed action) verb meaning 'to suffer, get hurt'.

examples.text: Я просто не хочу, чтобы кто-то пострадал.
examples.trans: I just do not want anyone to get hurt.

examples.text: Я просто не хочу, чтобы из-за нашей ссоры кто-то пострадал.
examples.trans: I just do not want anyone to get hurt because of our quarrel.

examples.text: Во время ремонта на кухне ни одно блюдо не пострадало.
examples.trans: During the repairs in the kitchen not a single dish suffered.

при.gloss: in the presence of, in front of; at, under

meanings.en: in the presence of, in front of (a person)
meanings.note: + prepositional: при нём, при детях
Secondary conversational sense ('at, attached to, during') (+ prepositional) used in spoken Russian dialogue.

examples.text: Зачем ты сейчас это при нём сказал?
examples.trans: Why did you just say that in front of him?

examples.text: Не говори об этом при детях.
examples.trans: Don't talk about this in front of the children.

meanings.note: Manner or predicative adverb in '-о' derived from the corresponding adjective stem, used in everyday speech to mean 'just'.
Secondary conversational sense ('easy') (это просто = it's easy) used in spoken Russian dialogue.

examples.text: Мы просто не хотели вас беспокоить. Всё отменим!
examples.trans: We just didn't want to bother you. We'll cancel it all!

meanings.note: Declinable feminine noun meaning 'work', changing its case ending across all six Russian grammatical cases to mark its role in the clause.
Secondary conversational sense ('job') used in spoken Russian dialogue.
+ instrumental; со before some consonant clusters: со всеми

examples.trans: Share it all equally with everyone, understand?

meanings.note: forms the superlative: самый главный = the most important
Secondary conversational sense ('the very') used in spoken Russian dialogue.

examples.trans: The most important thing is the people.
Do you know the main thing?

meanings.note: 'сейчас буду' = I'll be right there
Secondary conversational sense ('in a moment') used in spoken Russian dialogue.

examples.text: Конечно, помогу. Кто у вас сейчас начальник?
examples.trans: Of course I'll help. Who's your boss now?

meanings.note: Prefix 'с-' ('together' or 'down from') marks convergence or completion (stem 'лучайность'). Abstract feminine noun formed with the Slavic suffix '-ость' ('-ness, -ity') from the corresponding adjective. Common feminine noun meaning 'accident, chance' in everyday Russian.

examples.text: Поверь, это была просто глупая случайность!
examples.trans: Believe me, it was just a stupid accident!

examples.text: Поверь мне, это была просто глупая и нелепая случайность!
examples.trans: Believe me, it was just a foolish and ridiculous accident!

examples.text: Счастливая случайность помогла Максу получить работу на этой кухне.
examples.trans: A lucky chance helped Max get a job in this kitchen.

meanings.note: Prefix 'с-' ('together' or 'down from') marks convergence or completion (stem 'лушать'). Used in Russian as an imperfective verb expressing ongoing, habitual, or repeated action meaning 'to listen', forming an aspectual pair with 'послушать'.
the imperative 'слушай' starts a sentence, like 'look, ...'
Secondary conversational sense ('hello (on the phone)') ('Слушаю' = I'm listening) used in spoken Russian dialogue.

examples.text: Слушай, Самсон, я тут подумал. Твой начальник — такой опытный специалист.
examples.trans: Listen, Samson, I've been thinking. Your boss is such an experienced specialist.

собираться.gloss: to intend, to be about to; to gather

meanings.en: to intend, to plan, to be going to
meanings.note: Prefix 'с-' ('together' or 'down from') marks convergence or completion (stem 'обираться'). Used in Russian as an imperfective verb expressing ongoing, habitual, or repeated action meaning 'to intend', forming an aspectual pair with 'собраться'. The reflexive suffix '-ся'/'-сь' makes the action intransitive, reciprocal, or directed at the subject.
Secondary conversational sense ('to gather, to get ready') (pack or assemble) used in spoken Russian dialogue.

examples.text: Ну и что? Я всё равно переезжать собираюсь.
examples.trans: So what? I'm planning to move anyway.

meanings.note: Manner or predicative adverb in '-о' derived from the corresponding adjective stem, used in everyday speech to mean 'completely'.

examples.text: Совершенно верно, я мэр этого города.
examples.trans: Quite right, I am the mayor of this town.
This is a completely new car.

examples.text: Совершенно верно, я мэр этого города. И предложение у меня к вам такое.
examples.trans: Quite right, I am the mayor of this town. And my offer to you is this.

meanings.note: не специально = not on purpose, by accident
Secondary conversational sense ('specially, specifically') (for a particular purpose) used in spoken Russian dialogue.

examples.text: Ну перестаньте, вы же не специально!
examples.trans: Oh, stop it, you didn't do it on purpose!

examples.text: Я приготовил этот торт специально для вас.
examples.trans: I made this cake specially for you.
Are you doing this on purpose?

meanings.note: Invariable Russian adverb used to modify verbs or whole clauses with the sense 'here'.

examples.trans: The white one? Give me the keys.

meanings.note: Conversational Russian particle ('so') that adds modal nuance, emphasis, or discourse tone in spoken dialogue.
Secondary conversational sense ('like that, so') used in spoken Russian dialogue.

examples.trans: So I shouldn't wait for you?
So I shouldn't wait for you tonight?

meanings.note: Russian determiner/pronoun ('that') agreeing in gender, number, and case with the noun phrase it specifies.
in 'то, что ...' = 'what, the thing that'
Invariable Russian adverb used to modify verbs or whole clauses with the sense 'here'.

examples.trans: There's someone here to see you.

examples.text: Аркадий Борисович, извините, тут к вам человек.
examples.trans: Arkady Borisovich, I'm sorry, there's a man here to see you.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian pronoun ('you') whose case form reflects its grammatical role in the clause.
Secondary conversational sense ('other forms:  (gen/acc),  (dat),  (instr),  (prep)') used in spoken Russian dialogue.

examples.trans: Dad, did you bring any gum?

meanings.note: Russian preposition meaning 'at' that governs a specific oblique case on the following noun phrase.
Secondary conversational sense ('I have') (possession) used in spoken Russian dialogue.
Secondary conversational sense ('from (ask from someone)') (просить у кого) used in spoken Russian dialogue.

examples.text: Привет! Смотри, что у меня есть.

meanings.note: Prefix 'у-' marks departure, removal, or successful completion (stem 'вольнять'). Used in Russian as an imperfective verb expressing ongoing, habitual, or repeated action meaning 'to fire', forming an aspectual pair with 'уволить'.

examples.trans: You're firing me? Are you serious?

meanings.note: 'хватать за горло' = grab by the throat
Secondary conversational sense ('to be enough') (impersonal, with the genitive) used in spoken Russian dialogue.

examples.text: Почему он меня всё время за горло хватает?
examples.trans: Why does he keep grabbing me by the throat?

meanings.note: Manner or predicative adverb in '-о' derived from the corresponding adjective stem, used in everyday speech to mean 'well'.
Secondary conversational sense ('good, fine') (as an answer) used in spoken Russian dialogue.

examples.text: Хорошо, Виктор Петрович, я сейчас же всё переделаю заново!
examples.trans: All right, Viktor Petrovich, I will redo everything right now!

meanings.note: Russian imperfective verb expressing ongoing, habitual, or repeated action meaning 'to want', forming an aspectual pair with 'захотеть'; conjugates for person and number in the present/future and agrees in gender in the past tense.

examples.trans: If you don't want to, suit yourself.
They want to build a shopping centre there.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian pronoun ('what') whose case form reflects its grammatical role in the clause.
Secondary conversational sense ('that') (conjunction) used in spoken Russian dialogue.
Secondary conversational sense ('? = well?') used in spoken Russian dialogue.

examples.text: Привет! Смотри, что у меня есть.

meanings.note: + past tense: 'чтобы свидетели были'
Secondary conversational sense ('in order to') (+ infinitive) used in spoken Russian dialogue.

examples.trans: I'm calling to say thank you.
So that there are witnesses, Samson.

meanings.note: pointing at a thing or a situation; 'это' + noun = 'this is ...'
points at something: это моё = that's mine
Secondary conversational sense ('is') (linking word: главное — это народ) used in spoken Russian dialogue.
Secondary conversational sense ('other forms:') used in spoken Russian dialogue.

examples.trans: And this is for you. A toy car!

meanings.note: alone: 'я этого не хочу' = I don't want that

examples.trans: I'm sick of this communal flat.

examples.text: Меня уже тошнит от этой коммуналки! У нас труба уже неделю течёт.
examples.trans: I'm sick of this communal flat! Our pipe has been leaking for a week now.

meanings.note: меня = me (genitive/accusative), мне = to me (dative)
Secondary conversational sense ('other forms:  (gen/acc),  (dat),  (instr),  (prep)') used in spoken Russian dialogue.
